'''Satoshi Suzuki''' (24 June 1930 – 11 August 1991) was a Japanese [[mathematician]],<ref name="Maths History 1930 s389">{{cite web | title=Biography | website=Maths History | date=24 June 1930 | url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Suzuki_Satoshi/ | access-date=2 November 2023}}</ref> and a professor at [[Kyoto University]].<ref name="KAKEN e384">{{cite web | title=SUZUKI Satosi | website=KAKEN | url=https://nrid.nii.ac.jp/en/nrid/1000060026739/ | language=la | access-date=2 November 2023}}</ref>

">{{cite journal | last1=Furuya | first1=Mamoru | last2=Niitsuma | first2=Hiroshi | title=A note on regularity of Noetherian complete local rings of unequal characteristic | journal=Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series A, Mathematical Sciences | publisher=Project Euclid | volume=78 | issue=8 | date=1 October 2002 | issn=0386-2194 | doi=10.3792/pjaa.78.166 | page=| doi-access=free }}</ref>

* 5 articles<ref>[https://projecteuclid.org/journalArticle/Download?urlid=10.1215%2Fkjm%2F1250524601 On torsion of the module of differentials of a locality which is a complete intersection, 1965]</ref><ref>[https://projecteuclid.org/journalArticle/Download?urlid=10.1215%2Fkjm%2F1250524481 Note on formally projective modules, 1966]</ref><ref>[https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1968-019-04/S0002-9939-1968-0227161-3/S0002-9939-1968-0227161-3.pdf On the Flatness of Complete Formally Projective Modules, 1968]</ref><ref>[https://projecteuclid.org/journalArticle/Download?urlid=10.1215%2Fkjm%2F1250523904 Differential modules and derivations of complete discrete valuation rings, 1969]</ref><ref>Differentials of commutative rings, 1971 - Kingston, Ont., Queen's University</ref> written by Suzuki are cited in the textbook "Homologie des algèbres commutatives".<ref>{{cite book | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-51449-4 | doi=10.1007/978-3-642-51449-4 | title=Homologie des algèbres commutatives | date=1974 | last1=Andrè | first1=Michel | isbn=978-3-642-51450-0 }}</ref>

== Life ==
Satoshi Suzuki was born on 24 June 1930 in [[Nagoya]].  
He entered [[Kyoto University]] in 1949. 
He studied [[mathematics]] in his undergraduate cours. 
His adviser in graduate course was [[Yasuo Akizuki]] from 1953 to 1958,    
but his research ideas were developed by his own.  
He wrote a paper "Note on the existence of rational points"<ref>[https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/pjab1945/34/5/34_5_245/_article/-char/en/ Note on the existence of rational points,  Proceedings of the Japan Academy, 1958]</ref> published in the Proceedings of the Japan Academy in 1958.<ref>[https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Suzuki_Satoshi/ Satoshi Suzuki (1930 - 1991) - Biography - MacTutor History of Mathematics]</ref>

*1958 - 59 taught at Kyoto Women's University
*1959 - 61 taught at Momoyama Gakuin,  Sakai, Osaka
*1963    associate professor at Kyoto University
*1964    submitted his doctoral thesis "Some results on m-adic differentials" to Kyoto University
*1965 - 67    Purdue University, West Lafayette, Indiana, USA
*1967 - 68  Queen's University, Kingston, Canada
*1970    full professor at Kyoto University

[[Paulo Ribenboim]] wrote about Suzuki that "I was very interested in his work on differentials, especially the higher order differentials and I attended his lectures with profit. At my suggestion, Suzuki wrote up his lecture notes ....<ref>[https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Suzuki_Satoshi/ Satoshi Suzuki (1930 - 1991) - Biography - MacTutor History of Mathematics]</ref>"

*Some results on m-adic differentials, Kyoto University, 1964.
